chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from the one he mentioned, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: I heard him say:
The afraid is the one to whom fear did not leave a tongue he can speak with.

key_terms.لِسَانًا يَنْطِقُ بِهِ: A tongue with which to speak

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true fear (khawf) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishing true spiritual fear (*khawf*) from mere silence, defining it as a state where awe is so profound it physically silences the tongue. This aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of *khawf* as an active, overwhelming presence of the Divine in the heart that transcends verbal expression, often linked to the station of *muraqaba* (watchfulness).

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, ofALi ibn Muhammed al-Qasani, from the one he mentioned, from Abdullah bin Qasem al-Ju’fi, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: I heard him say:
The afraid is the one to whom fear did not leave a tongue he can speak with.
